I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is what fits our climate, my age, and the way I farm. I do not want to gamble on crops that need more labor, more market judgment, or more delicate management. Wheat and maize are familiar, easy to mechanize, and the input-output is steady enough for me to manage. I will use improved seed, put most of my fertilizer into wheat and maize because they respond reliably, irrigate wheat more carefully in key stages, and keep maize management simple after wheat harvest with no-tillage sowing to save time and effort. I will aim for stable yield first, not the highest possible yield, because at my age I care more about reducing risk and finishing the season smoothly.
